item_list.note: The 24 items below are the visible questionnaire items as supplied in the task brief. The public page describes the method and names only a handful of examples ('celibacy, childlessness, many children, imprisonment', 'Early marriage', 'Success in music'); the full item list is generated inside the app after birth data is submitted and is not published as a static list.
item_list.houses_published_evidence: The public rectification page was fetched and read in full. It contains no astrological house numbers anywhere, and states no mapping from any questionnaire item to any house. Verbatim, the only description of this stage is: 'it considers various options of the birth time taking into account predisposition to events. This refers to events or situations that do not occur to everybody, but which, as a rule, are well marked in the natal chart. For example, celibacy, childlessness, many children, imprisonment etc.'

inclusion_rule: An item is kept only if the matter it names is one of the nouns Lilly enumerates for a house (marriage, children, death, wealth/poverty, houses/lands, voyages beyond seas, religious men, profession, imprisonment/affliction). Items whose mapping would require adding a qualifier Lilly does not state are dropped, not inferred. Items requiring a judgement about temperament, appearance or self-perception are dropped separately under Work item 3.2.

planet_bridge.problem: A sourced item-to-house mapping still does not say WHICH planet's house to read. The origin publishes nothing on this, and Lilly's method of judging a matter by the lord of its house is far richer than a house-membership predicate and cannot be reduced to one without invention.
planet_bridge.rule: A 'yes' for an item mapped to house H is taken as evidence that house H is accidentally emphasised in the nativity, and is scored by the NUMBER OF PLANETS tenanting H at the candidate time. A 'no' is scored as the negation of the same quantity. 'unknown' contributes nothing.
planet_bridge.why_this_one: It is a single chart-independent rule, it uses exactly the planet-to-house vector already shown in Work item 1 to carry the narrowing information, and it commits to no per-item or per-chart choice that could be fitted after the fact.
planet_bridge.status: This is the one bridging choice not taken from a source. It is frozen here, before any scoring run, and it is the weakest link in the chain. It is stated as such in the report.
